## Speed

Changes to the hot path that keep the wire byte for byte and are measured by make bench and make bench-choices.

### The writer empties its accumulator every 32 bits

make bench-choices measures the writer's inner loop emptying its accumulator every 32 bits at 98 ns per 32-bit field with YJIT off and 59 ns with it on, against 133 ns and 89 ns for the whole 64-bit words the writer appends today, with the same bytes (the bench compares them before it measures). At 5-bit fields the gain is smaller (56 to 50 ns off, 34 to 27 ns on). Change WriteStream#put and #put_aligned_bytes, then re-measure make bench and update the README's table.

Already in the code: WriteStream appends whole 64-bit words (lib/serialize/core.rb, WriteStream#put); test_every_operation_from_every_start_offset and the corpus pin the bytes any change must keep.

Why it waits: Found by the design write-up; a change to the hot path lands on its own, behind the round-trip tests and the corpus.

## Public surface

What a caller can reach, held to IMPLEMENTING.md U15.

### Hide the names that are not the public surface

IMPLEMENTING.md U15: where the language can hide a name, it is hidden. Serialize::Encode (marked @api private), the declaration checks Serialize.number?, int_bounds?, fixed_params, precomputed_ok? and utf8_text?, and the constants INT32_MIN to UINT128_LIMIT, M64, RELATIVE_MAX, LAST_BOUNDED_MAX, TIERS, COMPRESSED_FLOAT_VALUES_MAX, FLOAT32_MAX, FLOAT32_OVERFLOW and TEXT_ENCODINGS are reachable today. Make them private with private_constant and private_class_method, keeping the names DESIGN.md lists as public.

Already in the code: DESIGN.md, The public surface, lists which names are public and says the rest are internal and promise nothing.

From: IMPLEMENTING.md U15, Exports beyond the reference operations
